hedges.reason: No gilt or sterling instrument is on the list, so I hedge the cause behind my hedge thesis instead: Starmer falling. In most worlds where Nandy is replaced, it is because a new Labour leader forms a new cabinet. That requires Starmer to leave office before 2027, and he is the listed leader most exposed to a party-internal removal.

A new PM, or a forced reset reshuffle, rebuilds the whole cabinet and rarely keeps every great office of state in place. The Home Office changing hands happens in the same worlds where DCMS changes hands.
Same mechanism. The Foreign Office is a senior post that an incoming PM usually hands out to reward allies or rivals, so Cooper being replaced goes with a full cabinet rebuild.

claims.reason: Nandy has already survived at least one 2026 reshuffle; the other markets reference new incumbents such as Jarvis at Defence. So Culture changing hands before year end most likely means a leadership change or a wholesale reset, and in that event the Home Secretary also changes. A mini-reshuffle aimed only at Culture is the smaller exception.

Starmer has already reshuffled without moving Nandy, so the main route to a new Culture Secretary is a new PM. That means Starmer leaves office before the other listed leaders, whose positions are fixed by election calendars or are not under party-internal leadership pressure in H2 2026.
